extraction.name: Stanford Question Answering Dataset (SQuAD)
extraction.description: A new reading comprehension dataset consisting of 100,000+ questions posed by crowdworkers on a set of Wikipedia articles, where the answer to each question is a segment of text from the corresponding reading passage.
extraction.creator: Pranav Rajpurkar, Jian Zhang, Konstantin Lopyrev, Percy Liang
extraction.citeAs: Pranav Rajpurkar, Jian Zhang, Konstantin Lopyrev, Percy Liang. SQuAD: 100,000+ Questions for Machine Comprehension of Text. 2016.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: We collect our dataset in three stages: curating passages, crowdsourcing question-answers on those passages, and obtaining additional answers.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: 2.6% of questions were marked unanswerable by at least one of the additional crowdworkers.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Project Nayuki’s Wikipedia’s internal PageRanks to obtain the top 10000 articles of English Wikipedia
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Extracted individual paragraphs, stripping away images, figures, tables, and discarding paragraphs shorter than 500 characters. Partitioned the articles randomly into a training set (80%), a development set (10%), and a test set (10%).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Crowdworkers were tasked with asking and answering up to 5 questions on the content of that paragraph. The questions had to be entered in a text field, and the answers had to be highlighted in the paragraph. Crowdworkers were encouraged to ask questions in their own words, without copying word phrases from the paragraph. For additional answers, crowdworkers were shown only the questions along with the paragraphs of an article, and asked to select the shortest span in the paragraph that answered the question.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Daemo platform, with Amazon Mechanical Turk as its backend
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Human performance (86.8%) is much higher than models. Mismatch occurs mostly due to inclusion/exclusion of non-essential phrases rather than fundamental disagreements about the answer.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Located in the United States or Canada, 97% HIT acceptance rate, minimum of 1000 HITs
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: SQuAD v1.0 and SQuAD v1.1 mentioned. Freely available at https://stanford-qa.com.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Questions with span-based answers are more constrained than the more interpretative questions found in more advanced standardized tests. 2.6% of questions were marked unanswerable.
